description: Given Prefect blocks holding credentials (SnowflakeCredentials/SnowflakeConnector, AirbyteConnection, or any other loaded via Block.load()), map each to the matching Orchestra connection type, referenced by name/${{ ENV.* }} in pipeline YAML — never inlined.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to an Orchestra pipeline task, focusing on how the SnowflakeConnector block's credentials should be represented (see files/snowflake_block_flow.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SNOWFLAKE task whose connection: references either a name_XXXXX connection or a ${{ ENV.* }} variable — never the literal account/user/password from the environment variable reads. warehouse/database/schema are not written as task parameters since they belong to the connection, not duplicated per task unless the source genuinely varies them.

assertions.text: The task uses the SNOWFLAKE integration
SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT / SNOWFLAKE_USER / SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env var names are not written as literal parameter values in the YAML

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra pipeline tasks, making sure the two AirbyteConnection blocks map to the correct Orchestra connection types (see files/airbyte_cloud_and_server_flow.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sync, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: Two tasks: one using an Airbyte Cloud-style connection (from the AirbyteConnection pointed at api.airbyte.com) and one using an Airbyte Server-style connection (from the AirbyteConnection pointed at the self-hosted internal host), each with the correct connection_id from the source, and neither block's credentials (the API key implied by api.airbyte.com auth, AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER/PASSWORD) written as literal values.

assertions.text: Both Airbyte tasks are distinguished from each other rather than collapsed into one identical connection type — the api.airbyte.com AirbyteConnection and the self-hosted AirbyteConnection map to different Orchestra connections
Connection ids 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 and 66666666-7777-8888-9999-000000000000 are carried over as the sync targets (as parameters, not as the connection: name itself)
AIRBYTE_SERVER_USER and AIRBYTE_SERVER_PASSWORD are not written as literal parameter values

evals.prompt: Convert this task to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how the Snowflake credentials behind SnowflakeConnector.load('snowflake-prod') should reach the running code (see files/rowcount_task.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task whose code reads the Snowflake credentials from the Snowflake connection *linked* on the Python connection — via orchestra.get_linked_connection("snowflake", ...) or the injected <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD> environment variables (e.g. SNOWFLAKE__PROD_12345__SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) — rather than the Snowflake account/user/password being copied into the Python connection's own Secrets or written into the YAML. A deleted or undecryptable linked connection is skipped silently, so the code must not assume the variables are present.

assertions.text: The converted code reads the warehouse credentials from a linked connection — get_linked_connection(...) or an injected SNOWFLAKE__<CONNECTION_ID>__SNOWFLAKE_* environment variable — rather than re-declaring them
No Snowflake account/user/password value is written into the YAML
The existing Snowflake connection is linked on the Python connection instead of its credentials being copied into that connection's Secrets — the warehouse credential stays in one place

Linked-credential environment variables are named <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD>, with a double underscore between parts and the field's ID (e.g. snowflake_password) as the last part — not a single underscore or the field's display label
The code tolerates a linked connection being skipped (deleted or undecryptable credentials) rather than assuming os.environ[...] is set — e.g. .get() or an explicit presence check

evals.prompt: We have 30-odd Prefect blocks across two workspaces to move. Does every one of them mean a manual Add Connection in the Orchestra UI, and can we automate the whole migration end to end? Don't call any live Orchestra tools — just tell us how you'd approach it.
evals.expected_output: Splits the answer by side. Orchestra side: connections can be created and maintained through the public API and the Orchestra MCP server as well as Settings -> Connections, so creating the connections is scriptable and each descriptive_name_NNNNN id is read back from the create response or by listing connections rather than copied from the UI. Prefect side: there is still no bulk export from Prefect's encrypted block store, so each secret value has to be recovered one at a time and the migration cannot be fully automated end to end — a script can create each connection as the value is recovered, except for secrets already in AWS Secrets Manager or Azure Key Vault, which can be read in place via Credential Store. Credential values are supplied at creation and never committed. Makes no live calls.

assertions.text: States that Orchestra connections can be created and managed through the public API and the Orchestra MCP server, not only through the UI
Says the name_NNNNN connection id is read back from the create response or by listing connections, rather than copied from the UI or invented
Does not claim the migration can be fully automated end to end — Prefect's block store still has no bulk export, so each secret value has to be recovered one at a time and that side stays manual
Keeps the credential rule: values are supplied at connection-creation time from the user or their secret store, never committed to a repo or a migration script
Makes no live Orchestra MCP tool calls and creates nothing in the workspace
